kind: development observation — posting hot-row benchmark for D-096
machine: MacBook Pro Mac14,10, Apple M2 Pro, arm64
load_average: ~5 while measuring (busy machine; numbers are development observations, not production capacity)
method: crates/sandbox-db/tests/posting_bench.rs, `cargo test --release -p sandbox-db --test posting_bench -- --nocapture`: N concurrent tasks each run whole transactions (begin, journal::post of a USD authorize, commit) against ONE project for 5s; postings/s and p50/p99 of the whole transaction

phases.label: before: journal insert only (code of 1a97f99, pre-D-096)
D-096 with 16 stripes per account (this commit)

reading: The one-row-per-account design flattened at ~1,100 postings/s from 8 concurrent tasks (lock-wait dominated; p99 286ms at 64). 16 stripes (hash of the entry id) spread the rows: 5,484/s at 64 — about 5x the unstriped number and ~70% of the no-balance baseline; the residual gap is the upsert's own work plus ~1/16 same-stripe collisions. Baseline scaling continues past 64 only because journal inserts never contend.
